The nonstandard strict monotonicity lemma is proved via log-concavity of 1/j! composition weights, closure under convolution of Toeplitz TP2 kernels, and strict monotone-likelihood-ratio comparison from an added maximal possible fiber. Positive endpoint follows from existence of partitions with two nonsingleton blocks. Inclusion–exclusion gives the fixed-k exponential singleton asymptotics and unique macroscopic threshold. Exact-rational exhaustive restricted growth enumeration n<=9 and Stirling checks k<=15,n<=320 corroborate but do not establish the theorem.

value.rationale: Uniform partitions into a fixed number of blocks are a canonical conditioned occupancy model. The new structural strict monotonicity classifies all singleton-to-size-s covariance signs and prohibits multiple reversals at every finite n,k. The fixed-k macroscopic cutoff rho_k separates two dependence regimes and is unlike the known unconditioned Lambert-W cutoff; an exact zero with genuine dependence illustrates probabilistic importance. The nontrivial TP2 convolution argument and sharp asymptotic make this a meaningful structure theorem, not merely a sample calculation or tautological Stirling substitution.
